Published online:
2 September 2026

Geographic focus:
Europe (North West Europe, ARA hub: Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp), with secondary references to Middle East, Russia, Ukraine

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — References June 2022 record margins and recent Tuesday/Wednesday price moves
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Ongoing conflict disruptions and Rhine water level impacts remain active, implying near-term supply tightness
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
European gasoline refinery margins nearly broke the all-time record on 2 September 2026, reaching $62.07/bbl for Eurobob E5 barges vs Brent. The surge is driven by a confluence of supply-side shocks: refinery attacks in the Middle East and Russia tightening global refined product availability, combined with a hot, dry European summer that reduced Rhine river water levels and constrained barge deliveries into the ARA hub. The combination brings margins within touching distance of the June 2022 post-Ukraine-invasion record of $62.10/bbl.

Relevance: YES — Supply is being squeezed from multiple angles: geopolitical attacks on refining infrastructure globally and Rhine logistics constraints reducing deliveries into Europe's primary refined products hub.
Severity score: 78 — Near-record margins reflect acute physical supply tightness; the convergence of geopolitical and weather-driven disruptions is severe and multi-sourced.

Q07. Is the content describing effects very directly impacting Europe and/or European energy markets?
Relevance: YES — The article is explicitly focused on European gasoline markets, ARA hub pricing, Rhine logistics, and European refinery margins.
Severity score: 88 — Near-record European gasoline crack spreads with direct, immediate pricing impact on the ARA physical market, the benchmark for North West European refined products.
